newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges no quick conclusions in N.Y. plot.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges no quick conclusions in N.Y. plot.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday praised police for foiling an alleged bomb plot by Middle Easterners but said it was too early to draw conclusions about the case.

"We have worked very hard in this country to increase our capacity to deal with terrorism, it is something we take very seriously, and we will continue to do that," Clinton told reporters at the White House.

"But I think it's important not to reach conclusions before we have ironclad evidence to support them," he said, trying to dampen speculation that the suspects may be linked to international terrorism. "The main thing we need to do is to thank the law enforcement officials for what they did and to continue to heighten our vigilance."

Two men charged in the alleged conspiracy were shot and wounded by police in a dawn raid on Thursday in New York City in which five pipe bombs were discovered. The bombs allegedly were to be used for an attack in the city's subway system.
A third man was also being questioned by agents from the Joint Terrorist Task Force of local, state and federal agencies, officials said.

Authorities said at least one of two suspects named in court documents had a Jordanian passport. They said Gazi Ibrahim Abu Mezer, 23, had allegedly been accused in Israel "of being a member of a known terrorist organisation."
